items.statement:
The actual determinant-conditioned Gaussian mixtures have nonnegative measurable Lebesgue-integrable densities of mass one. P_b(dx)=q_b(x)\,dx,\qquad q_b\ge0,\quad q_b\in L^1(dx),\quad\int q_b(x)\,dx=1,\qquad b\in\{-1,+1\}. Exactly \(n\in\mathbb N,\ n\ge3\) and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge4\), including both endpoints and odd dimensions. Every \(n/2\) is a real exponent. \(\mu\) is the canonical full-orthogonal Haar probability and \(
u_b=2\mu\!estriction\{\det O=b\}\). The actual mixture is \(P_b=
u_b\mathrm{bind}\gamma\), where \(\gamma_O=\mathcal N(0,A_O^{-1})\). The source density \(p_b\) is determined only Lebesgue-a.e. We choose the literal average \(q_b\) below and certify it by equality of actual measures. No pointwise equality to a different arbitrary source representative is asserted. Pointwise inner absolute integrability, measurability, matrix positivity, actual mixture probability, outer L1, normalization and the measure identity are proved inside the theorem. None is a caller hypothesis; totalized Bochner integration supplies no fallback value. assumptions: Exactly \(n\in\mathbb N,\ n\ge3\) and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R,\ \kappa\ge4\), including both endpoints and odd dimensions. Every \(n/2\) is a real exponent.

\(\mu\) is the canonical full-orthogonal Haar probability and \(\nu_b=2\mu\!\restriction\{\det O=b\}\). The actual mixture is \(P_b=\nu_b\mathrm{bind}\gamma\), where \(\gamma_O=\mathcal N(0,A_O^{-1})\).

The source density \(p_b\) is determined only Lebesgue-a.e. We choose the literal average \(q_b\) below and certify it by equality of actual measures. No pointwise equality to a different arbitrary source representative is asserted.
